# jev-writer

> Finds which qualities of your writing actually predict engagement. It analyses
> published posts and never generates them; the underlying model cannot write.

jev-writer rates every post you have published against a pre-registered
rubric using Jev, TypeSafe AI's System One model, then tests those ratings
against your real engagement data. It reports findings in plain language and
withholds conclusions when the sample is too small to support them.

## What it is

- A command-line tool and agent skill, MIT licensed, Node >= 20, 67 tests.
- Bring your own key: Vercel AI Gateway, OpenRouter, or TypeSafe direct.
- LinkedIn is the first adapter; rubric packs make other platforms user-space files.

## Running it

The package is not published to npm. Both of these work:

```
npx github:Kaos599/jev-writer doctor
npx github:Kaos599/jev-writer run ./exports
```

Or from a clone: `git clone https://github.com/Kaos599/jev-writer`, `npm
install`, then `node src/cli.mjs doctor` and `node src/cli.mjs run ./exports`.
`npx jev-writer` alone does not resolve.

Commands: `doctor` (node, keys, packs, one live call), `build <dir>` (parse
exports into a corpus), `rate` (rate the corpus, resumable), `analyze`
(correlate against outcomes, write the report), `dashboard` (render the report
as one HTML page), `run <dir>` (all of them in order).

Output goes to `jev-out/`, overridable with `JEV_WRITER_OUT`: `corpus.jsonl`,
`ratings.jsonl`, `report.json`, `dashboard.html`. The last two embed the full
text of every post, so the directory is gitignored.

The agent skill installs with:

```
npx skills add Kaos599/jev-writer --skill jev-writer
```

## What makes it different from an LLM rating your posts

- Jev returns calibrated probability distributions rather than generated scores,
  so a rubric whose confidence sits near 0.5 across a corpus can be detected as
  broken rather than silently reported.
- Every question is pre-registered in git as primary or exploratory before any
  result is seen, and the commit timestamp is the evidence.
- Below 25 posts with outcome data the tool refuses to correlate at all and
  shows descriptive statistics only.
- Headline results are re-tested as partial correlations controlling for
  publication date, because a rated dimension and an outcome that both drift
  over time will correlate for no reason. The false-discovery correction runs on
  the controlled p-value, not the raw one.
- Permutation tests and bootstrap intervals are seeded and the seed is reported,
  so any finding is reproducible by anyone holding the same data.
- Countable features such as length, emoji, hashtags and posting cadence are
  computed in code and compete with the model's judgments on equal footing.

## Two outcomes it keeps separate

- reach rate = impressions divided by follower count at post time. Did the
  platform distribute it?
- conversion rate = engagements divided by impressions. Given that people saw
  it, did the writing work? This is unconfounded by follower count and feed luck.

## Importing it as a library

The `exports` map in `package.json` is the stable surface; deep paths into
`src/` do not resolve from outside the package.

- `jev-writer` - everything below, re-exported
- `jev-writer/stats.mjs` - correlations, permutation tests, the power gate
- `jev-writer/report.mjs` - the plain-language report layer
- `jev-writer/dashboard.mjs` - `buildDashboard(report, opts)`, returns HTML
- `jev-writer/rubrics/pack.mjs` - pack format and `validatePack`
- `jev-writer/rubrics/linkedin-post.mjs` - the shipped pack and its directions
- `jev-writer/adapters/linkedin.mjs` - LinkedIn export parsing

## Key files

- README: https://github.com/Kaos599/jev-writer#readme
- Contributor notes and known traps: AGENTS.md
- Agent skill and its five reference files: skills/jev-writer/
- Rubric pack format and validation: src/rubrics/pack.mjs
- Statistics and the power gate: src/stats.mjs
- Plain-language report layer: src/report.mjs
- Dashboard renderer: src/dashboard.mjs
- LinkedIn export adapter: src/adapters/linkedin.mjs
